materials.name: Plaster dabs (dot and dab adhesive)
materials.source: λ: BR 443 (2006) 4.7.1, which tabulates plaster dabs at 0.43 W/(m·K), 15 mm thick and 0.20 of the face. c: BR 443 (2019) 16 (Gypsum, plasters and renders, plasterboard). ρ: TODO(verify) — BR 443 gives the conductivity, thickness and area fraction of a dab but no density, so this carries the same 1300 kg/m³ as set gypsum plaster, which is what a dab is. Beware the figure on an adhesive datasheet: the density quoted there is usually the dry powder in the bag, around 500 kg/m³, and not the set material. μ: EVIDENCED — the conventional value for gypsum plaster, agreeing across the independent public sources consulted; not read from BS EN ISO 10456:2007 Table 3.
materials.notes: Used as the bridging member of a dot-and-dab cavity rather than as a layer in its own right. Its thickness is the cavity's, since the dab spans it.

materials.name: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) board
materials.source: λ: TODO(verify). c: BR 443 (2019) 16 (Mineral wool, expanded and extruded polystyrene). μ: EVIDENCED — the conventional value for expanded polystyrene, agreeing across the independent public sources consulted; μ is grade-dependent and ours sits high. EUMEPS's EPS White Book, tabulating EN 13163 Annex D.2 as revised, gives μ 20–40 for EPS 30–80, 30–70 for EPS 90–150 and 40–100 for EPS 200 and above. Our 60 is inside the EPS 90–150 band and outside the EPS 70 one, so it does not suit a common wall board. Not read from BS EN ISO 10456:2007 Table 3. See VERIFY.md row V31.
materials.notes: c 1450 J/(kg·K) is BR 443 16, "Mineral wool, expanded and extruded polystyrene". Generic value only; lambda is product-specific and declared to BS EN 13163. Check c and mu against BS EN ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 (EPS).
